title: Thomas Christians
hook: Christians in Kerala trace their church to the apostle Thomas

segments.voice: Yesterday: Armenia, a man pulled alive from a pit, and your line, light from a pit.

"Let us also go, that we may die with him." That's Thomas, in John's Gospel. Jesus has decided to head back toward Judea, where people had just tried to stone him, and the other disciples hesitate. Thomas says, in effect: fine, then we all go. Later, the same Thomas refuses to believe Jesus is risen until he can touch the wounds, and the nickname sticks: doubting Thomas. But on the southwest coast of India, in Kerala, there are Christians who remember him differently: as the apostle who came all the way to their shore.

Start with what the Bible says, and what it doesn't. The book of Acts names Thomas among the apostles praying together in Jerusalem after the ascension. After that, the New Testament goes silent. It never says where he went. Later writers filled the silence. The Acts of Thomas, a book that is not part of the Bible, tells it like a folk tale. The apostles divide the world between them, and India falls to Thomas. He doesn't want to go, so, in the story, the risen Jesus sells him to a merchant as a carpenter. An Indian king hands him money to build a palace. Thomas gives it all to the poor, and when the king demands to see his palace, the answer is that it's being built in heaven. The historian Eusebius records a different tradition: Thomas was sent to Parthia, the land of the Persians. The old voices don't agree on the map, but they agree on the direction: east. In Kerala, the Christians who call themselves Thomas Christians hold that he landed on their coast, preached, founded churches, and died a martyr in India. That's their tradition, kept in their own memory and in churches named for him. Historians weigh it differently, and the texts alone can't settle it. And notice who tradition sends to the far edge. Not the one with the keys. The one the nickname calls the doubter, who, when he finally saw the wounds, said, in the King James words: "My Lord and my God." On this path the story has mostly headed west, to Rome and beyond. Here is a thread running the other way.

segments.voice: Bring India to mind; if you've never seen pictures of Kerala, just hold the name. Christians there live alongside neighbors of other faiths, and they belong to more than one church. If you pray, pray for the church in India by name, and for its neighbors too; if you don't, hold them in mind a while and wish them peace.
